lines.text: Seismic surveys said the drill would hit a layer of basalt, at around seven kilometres down.
The plan was to go through it, all the way to fifteen kilometres.
They passed seven kilometres, then seven and a half.
No basalt. Just gneiss, an old, granite-like rock, all the way through.
That's the kind of thing you only learn by going there.
And yet something down there really did make those waves bounce.
So what had they been bouncing off?
The full video has the answer.
